overview.aftermathUnread: The overview could not be read again, so whether the capture was saved is not known here. Open Versions to see the library.

overview.aftermathMore_one: The library now holds {n} more version(s) than before. The capture may have been saved.
overview.aftermathMore_other: The library now holds {n} more version(s) than before. The capture may have been saved.

overview.overviewUnreadable: the server sent an overview this page cannot read

overview.staleAt: {heading}. The figures below were read at {time}.

overview.interrupted_one: One restore operation did not finish. Open Restore to resolve it.
overview.interrupted_other: {n} restore operations did not finish. Open Restore to resolve them.
overview.captureTip: Captures every object every available adapter can see into a new version. Nothing in the world changes.
overview.liveNote: The server keeps a world capture for 30 s after it was last read. Open Objects to capture the current world.
overview.versionsShare: Versions on this map, of all maps
overview.noVersions: No versions yet on this map.
overview.noVersionsHint: Capture the current server setup to create your first one.
overview.workingShare: Working adapters, of those whose addon is installed

overview.noAdapters: No adapters are registered, so there is nothing to capture.
overview.migrationsShare: Migrations targeting this map, of all
overview.capturingNote: Capturing the world. Every available adapter reads its objects; nothing in the world changes.

versions.title: Versions
versions.wantNotLoaded: Version {id} is not among the first {cap} versions loaded.
versions.wantMissing: Version {id} is not in the library.
versions.previousTruncated: Only the first {cap} versions are loaded, so the one before this cannot be known.
versions.previousLoading: The library has not finished loading, so the one before this is not known yet.
versions.compareNeedsPair: Select two versions, or pin a base with B and select another.
versions.previousNoneHere: There is no earlier version captured by this server on this map.
versions.rereadFailed: Reading the library again failed; Refresh reads it once more.
versions.rereadNone: The library was read again; it holds no new version.
versions.rereadNew_one: The library was read again and now holds a version it did not hold before: {ids}.
versions.rereadNew_other: The library was read again and now holds {n} versions it did not hold before, {ids}.
versions.captureUnconfirmed: The server did not confirm the capture. It may still have run; nothing is sent again.
versions.exportUnconfirmed: The server did not confirm the export. It may still have run; nothing is sent again.
versions.cloneUnconfirmed: The server did not confirm the clone. It may still have run; nothing is sent again.
versions.captureUnread: The server confirmed the capture, but its report could not be read. The library was read again.
versions.exportDone: Exported {id} to {file}. It is on the server, in {dir}; this page cannot download it.
versions.exportDoneFolder: Exported {id} to {file}. It is on the server, in the export folder; this page cannot download it.
versions.exportUnread: The server confirmed the export of {id}, but its reply could not be read. The package is in the server's export folder.
versions.cloneDone: Cloned {from} as {id}. Nothing in the world changed.
versions.cloneUnread: The server confirmed the clone of {id}, but its reply could not be read. The library was read again.
versions.emptyBody: Capture the current server setup to create your first version.
versions.partialFailure: {heading}. Only {n} of {total} versions arrived; what is shown is incomplete.
versions.duplicateIds_one: One id is held by more than one snapshot file ({ids}), and each is listed once: the server can address only one file per id. Check those files on the server.
versions.duplicateIds_other: {n} ids are held by more than one snapshot file ({ids}), and each is listed once: the server can address only one file per id. Check those files on the server.
versions.truncatedNote: Showing the first {n} of {total} versions. Search, filters and sorting cover the loaded versions only.
versions.cloneConfirmBody: A second version with exactly the same contents will be added to the library, under a new id. Its origin is kept as it is.
versions.selectHint: {base} pins a base; every version you then select is compared against it. Or move with {move} and toggle a second one with {toggle}.
versions.unreadableNote: This file could not be read. It is listed rather than hidden so a version you can see on disk never silently vanishes.
versions.sinceFirst: The first readable version on {map}. Nothing earlier to compare with.
versions.dangling_one: {n} group member points at an object that is not in this version.
versions.dangling_other: {n} group members point at an object that is not in this version.
versions.noGroupClaim: This version makes no claim about groups.
versions.previousElsewhere: This version came from elsewhere, so its identities do not line up with this server's history.
versions.previousNone: No earlier version was captured by this server on {map}.
versions.exportDoneNote: The package is on the server, at {path}. This page cannot download it: copy it off the server over FTP or the host's file manager. Another server imports it from its own import folder.
versions.restoreInspecting: This version is still being inspected, so whether it can be restored here is not known yet.
versions.restoreInspectFailed: This version could not be inspected, so whether it can be restored here is not known. Inspect it again first.
versions.exportStillWaiting: The export is still waiting for the server.
versions.cloneStillWaiting: The clone is still waiting for the server.
versions.restoreForeign: This version came from another Vetra server. Its object identities belong to that server, so it cannot be restored here. Use Migrate instead.
versions.restoreUnverified: This version says it came from this server, but there is no record of exporting it. The record may have been deleted, or the contents changed after export. It cannot be restored, and cannot be turned on later; re-export the original if you need a package you can restore. Migrate still works.
versions.restoreUnattributed: This version does not record which server captured it, so it cannot be restored here. Migrate still works.
versions.restoreOtherMap: That version belongs to another map and cannot be restored here.
versions.spineHidden: Version spine hidden: it only means something in capture order
versions.deltaTitle: Object count change since the previous version on this map

compare.blockedSame: That is the same version twice. Select two different versions.
compare.blockedUnreadable: One of these versions could not be read, so there is nothing to compare.
compare.blockedMaps: These versions were captured on different maps ({from} and {to}). A comparison is always within one map.
compare.truncated: Only the first {n} changes were loaded. The bridge caps a comparison at {cap} rows; the totals above are exact.
compare.sameBody: These two versions describe the same world. Every object, group and setting matches.
compare.noMatchBody: Nothing among {n} changes matches the current filter.
compare.selectChange: Select a change. Arrow keys move through the list.
compare.groupNotItemised: Group changes are listed, not itemised: the server inspects modified objects only.
compare.wholeAdded: A whole object was added, so there is no field list. It exists in only one of the two versions.
compare.wholeModified: A whole object was modified, so there is no field list. It exists in only one of the two versions.
compare.wholeRemoved: A whole object was removed, so there is no field list. It exists in only one of the two versions.

import.unreadableList: the server sent a package list this page cannot read
import.unreadablePackage: the server sent a package this page cannot read
import.gateDuplicate: Already imported as '{id}'. Use Clone on that version for another copy.
import.gateNotChecked: This package has not been checked yet: the folder holds too many to check at once. Check it first.
import.originTextForeign: This package says it was made on another Vetra server. Inspecting it changes nothing here, and it can be used as a migration source. Restore is unavailable because the object identities inside it belong to that server, not this one.
import.originTextUnverified: This package says it was made on this server, but there is no record of exporting it. The record may have been deleted, or the contents changed after export. Inspecting it changes nothing here, and it can be used as a migration source. Restore is unavailable and cannot be turned on later; re-export the version if you need one you can restore.
import.originTextUnattributed: This package does not record which Vetra installation captured the version inside it. Inspecting it changes nothing here, and it can be used as a migration source. Restore is unavailable.
import.originTextSame: This server exported this exact package, and still has the record of doing so. Restore is available.
import.restoreBlockedForeign: Its identities belong to another server
import.restoreBlockedUnverified: There is no record of exporting this exact content
import.restoreBlockedUnattributed: This package does not say where it came from
import.restoreBlockedAdapter: An adapter it needs is unavailable
import.confirmNotRestorableForeign: It cannot be restored on this server: its identities belong to another server. It can be compared and used as a migration source.
import.confirmNotRestorableUnverified: It cannot be restored on this server: there is no record of exporting this exact content. It can be compared and used as a migration source.
import.confirmNotRestorableUnattributed: It cannot be restored on this server: this package does not say where it came from. It can be compared and used as a migration source.
import.confirmNotRestorableAdapter: It cannot be restored on this server: an adapter it needs is unavailable. It can be compared and used as a migration source.
import.emptyTitle: No packages in the import folder
import.emptyBody: Copy a .vetra.json package into the server's import folder, then refresh. The exact path is in the panel beside this list.
import.title: Import Version
import.previousReading: The list below is the previous reading of the folder.
import.truncated: The folder holds more packages than one reply can carry; the first {n} are listed. Move some out of {dir} to see the rest.
import.confirmBody: A new version will be added to the library from {file}.
import.confirmWorld: Nothing in the world changes. The package file stays where it is.
import.doneNotRestorable: It cannot be restored on this server; it can be compared and used as a migration source.
import.doneUnread: The server confirmed the import of {file}, but its reply could not be read. The library and this folder were read again.
import.unconfirmed: The server did not confirm the import of {file}. It may still have run; nothing is sent again.
import.rereadBoth: This folder and the library were read again.
import.folderHelp: Copy a package into this folder on the server, over FTP or the host's file manager, then press Refresh. This page cannot upload a file.
import.folderNames: Only names of lowercase letters, digits, - and _ ending in {ext} are listed. The package file stays there after an import.
import.exportsNote: Export writes a package to {dir}. Copy it from there to another server's import folder.
import.unreadableFile: This file could not be read.
import.checkNote: A listing opens a limited number of packages at a time and skipped this one. Checking reads this file alone.
import.duplicateNote: This package is in the library as {id}. Use Clone on that version for another copy.
import.integrityNote: The contents match the checksum recorded in the package, so nothing was damaged in transit. This does not identify who created the file.

objects.membersTooMany: A group holds at most {max} objects; {n} are selected.

objects.objectUnreadable: the server sent an object this page cannot read
objects.intentBadGroup: The link named the group {name}, which is not a group id. Every object is shown.
objects.intentBadAdapter: The link named the adapter {name}, which is not an adapter id. Every object is shown.

objects.intentEmptyAdapter: The adapter {id} reports no object in the world right now.

objects.writeNoteUnknown: The server's answer did not confirm the group. It may have been created; the world has been read again, so the Group column shows what the server holds.
objects.emptyWorldBody: No adapter reports any object on this map right now. Capture the world again if you have just changed something.
objects.noMatchBody_one: No object among {n} object matches the current search or filters.
objects.noMatchBody_other: No object among {n} objects matches the current search or filters.
objects.refreshTip: Re-captures the world: the server walks every object of every adapter again, and other administrators' views of it become stale.
objects.confirmBody_one: Creates the group {name} from {n} selected object.
objects.confirmBody_other: Creates the group {name} from {n} selected objects.
objects.confirmNote: The server reads each one again from its own capture; nothing on screen is taken as authority, and an object that has left the world is left out. Nothing in the world changes.
objects.createdWithMissing_one: Created the group {name} ({id}) with {n} object; {missing} selected were no longer in the world.
objects.createdWithMissing_other: Created the group {name} ({id}) with {n} objects; {missing} selected were no longer in the world.
objects.createdUnknown: Created the group {name}. The server's answer does not say which group is the new one; Groups lists them all.
objects.partialArrived_one: {heading}. Only {n} of {total} objects arrived; what is shown is incomplete.
objects.partialArrived_other: {heading}. Only {n} of {total} objects arrived; what is shown is incomplete.
objects.truncated: Showing the first {n} of {total} objects. The server searches and filters every object, so narrow the search or filters to reach the rest.
objects.staleHeading: The world was captured again while loading
objects.staleBody: Another read re-captured the world while this list was loading, so what had arrived is out of date. Read it again.
objects.inspectorHint: {ctrl} click or {space} adds one to the selection, {shift} click or {shiftArrows} a range. A selection becomes a group.
objects.inspectLoading: Reading the object from the world
objects.noProperties: The adapter recorded no properties for this object.
objects.hiddenCount_one: {n} hidden by the search or filters
objects.hiddenCount_other: {n} hidden by the search or filters
objects.newGroupNote: The server reads each object again from its own capture; one that has left the world is left out.

groups.anchorIntro: Only the anchor of {name} moves. The objects stay where they are; the group records them relative to the new anchor.
groups.answerReplaced: {message} The server sent nothing else with this answer, so the change may still have been made; the list was read again.
groups.cancelEsc: Cancelled with Esc. Nothing was sent to the server.
groups.cancelNoResult: The placement ended without a result. Nothing was sent to the server.
groups.cancelNoSurface: The ghosts could not be placed on the surface. Nothing was sent to the server.
groups.cancelOther: {reason} Nothing was sent to the server.
groups.cancelPage: Cancelled by the page. Nothing was sent to the server.
groups.cancelPlain: Cancelled. Nothing was sent to the server.
groups.cancelWorld: Cancelled in the world. Nothing was sent to the server.
groups.closeWhileRunning: The server is running it. Closing this would not stop it.
groups.ctlPlaceAnchor: Place the anchor where you aim, and confirm
groups.deleteBody: This removes the grouping, not the props. Nothing in the world changes.
groups.deleteIrreversible_one: The group document {name} is deleted and its {n} member is released. The objects themselves stay exactly where they are.
groups.deleteIrreversible_other: The group document {name} is deleted and its {n} members are released. The objects themselves stay exactly where they are.
groups.deleteUnconfirmed: The delete was not confirmed. It may have run; the list was read again.
groups.emptyBody: A group is a set of objects that move, migrate and restore together. Select objects in the Objects section to create one.
groups.emptyGroupBody: It has no members, and members cannot be added to an existing group from here. Delete it, or create a new group from objects in the Objects section.
groups.lastListShown: {heading}. {body} The list shown is the last one the server sent.
groups.listUnreadable: the server sent a group list this page cannot read
groups.loadingGroups: Reading the groups on this map
groups.membersTruncated: Showing the first {shown} of {n} members. The server sorts and filters all of them; only these arrived.
groups.moveIntro: Every member of {name} moves with its anchor, in the world, under the server's mutation lock. If one member cannot move, the server moves the others back.
groups.moveMissing_one: {n} member does not resolve. The server refuses to move a group while any member is missing. Prune them, or restore the objects, first.
groups.moveMissing_other: {n} members do not resolve. The server refuses to move a group while any member is missing. Prune them, or restore the objects, first.
groups.moveNoMembers: This group has no members. The server refuses to move it: there is nothing to move.
groups.moveUnknown: The server could not resolve this group's members when it last listed them. It refuses the move if any member is missing.
groups.nameControl: A name cannot hold control characters.
groups.noMembersBody_one: Nothing among {n} member matches these filters.
groups.noMembersBody_other: Nothing among {n} members matches these filters.
groups.notInLibrary: Group {id} is not in this map's group library.
groups.phasePlacing: Placing in the world. This page comes back when you confirm or cancel there.
groups.phasePreviewing: Asking the server for a preview at your aim
groups.phaseSent: Sent. Waiting for the server's answer.
groups.placeCancelBlocked: The placement runs in the world: Esc there cancels it. The server's answer comes back here.
groups.pruneBody: Members that no longer resolve to anything in the world are removed from the group. The server resolves them again first, so the number it removes can differ from this count.
groups.pruneIrreversible_one: {n} member is removed from this group's document. Nothing in the world is deleted.
groups.pruneIrreversible_other: {n} members are removed from this group's document. Nothing in the world is deleted.
groups.pruneNothing: Nothing to prune: every member resolves.
groups.pruneUnconfirmed: The prune was not confirmed. It may have run; the list was read again.
groups.pruneUnknown: The server did not resolve this group's members, so what is missing is not known. Refresh first.
groups.reasonAdapterMissing: the adapter that owned it is not loaded
groups.reasonCrossSession: recorded in an earlier server session, so it cannot be matched now
groups.renameBody: A group name is a label. It does not affect membership.
groups.renameUnconfirmed: The rename was not confirmed. It may have run; the list was read again.
groups.resolutionMissing: Some members no longer resolve to anything in the world. That is normal after a restart for session-scoped objects.
groups.resolutionUnknown: The server could not read the world when it listed the groups, so it did not resolve any member. Refresh to ask again.
groups.tiltAnchor: The placement sets a position and a yaw only, so this anchor's pitch ({pitch}) and roll ({roll}) become 0.
groups.tiltMove: The placement sets a position and a yaw only, so this anchor's pitch ({pitch}) and roll ({roll}) become 0, which also levels the objects in the world.
groups.title: Groups
groups.truncated_one: The server sent {n} group, the most one reply holds. Others on this map are not listed, and search covers these only.
groups.truncated_other: The server sent {n} groups, the most one reply holds. Others on this map are not listed, and search covers these only.
groups.unconfirmed: The server did not confirm the result.
groups.unknownSent: It may still have run. Nothing will be sent again from here; the screen reloads what the server actually holds.
groups.unknownWorld: This page stopped waiting while you were in the world. If you confirmed the placement there, it was sent and may have run. Nothing will be sent again from here; the screen reloads what the server actually holds.

migration.addInert: The last request was not confirmed. Close, and check the list first.
migration.addUnitIntro: A unit is one group of the source version {version}, placed and materialized as one. Each group can be a unit once.
migration.addUnitUnconfirmed: The new unit was not confirmed. It may have been added; the list was read again.
migration.allGroupsUsed: Every group in the source version is already a unit of this migration.
migration.allRemoved: Everything this unit created was removed again. Nothing remains in the world.
migration.alreadyPlaced: This unit is already placed. Confirming records the new position instead.
migration.askingPreview: Asking the server for a preview.
migration.cleanupBody: These objects were created by this migration and could not be removed. Remove them by hand before retrying.
migration.cleanupLeftMore_one: Materialize failed, and cleanup was incomplete: {n} object it created is still in the world ({list}, and {more} more). Remove them by hand before retrying.
migration.cleanupLeftMore_other: Materialize failed, and cleanup was incomplete: {n} objects it created are still in the world ({list}, and {more} more). Remove them by hand before retrying.
migration.cleanupLeft_one: Materialize failed, and cleanup was incomplete: {n} object it created is still in the world ({list}). Remove them by hand before retrying.
migration.cleanupLeft_other: Materialize failed, and cleanup was incomplete: {n} objects it created are still in the world ({list}). Remove them by hand before retrying.

migration.createTargetFixed: Its target map can never change: to migrate onto another map, create the migration while the server runs that map.
migration.createUnconfirmed: The new migration was not confirmed. It may have been created; the list was read again.
migration.createdRemoved_one: Materialize failed. {n} object was created and all were removed again; nothing remains.
migration.createdRemoved_other: Materialize failed. {n} objects were created and all were removed again; nothing remains.
migration.ctlMoveAnchor: Move the anchor to where you aim
migration.deleteBody: Deleting works from any map. Its target group and the objects it created are not touched.
migration.deleteIrreversible_one: The migration document {name} is deleted, with its {n} unit. Objects it already materialized stay in the world.
migration.deleteIrreversible_other: The migration document {name} is deleted, with its {n} units. Objects it already materialized stay in the world.
migration.deleteUnconfirmed: The delete was not confirmed. It may have run; the list was read again.
migration.emptyBody: A migration moves a setup captured on one map onto another. Start one from a version in the Versions section.
migration.lastFailedLeft_one: The last materialize failed and left {n} object this unit created in the world. They are still recorded here.
migration.lastFailedLeft_other: The last materialize failed and left {n} objects this unit created in the world. They are still recorded here.
migration.lastListShown: {heading}. {body} The list shown is the last one the server sent.
migration.listUnreadable: the server sent a migration list this page cannot read
migration.matBlockers_one: The server's preview lists one blocker, and it refuses to materialize while any remain.
migration.matBlockers_other: The server's preview lists {n} blockers, and it refuses to materialize while any remain.
migration.matMaterialized: Already materialized. Undoing a completed migration is not part of this build.
migration.matNotReady: The server's preview says this unit is not ready.
migration.matPlaceFirst: Place the unit first: its objects are created at the placed position.
migration.matPreviewFailed: The preview did not load, so what would be created is not known. Refresh the preview.
migration.matWaitingPreview: Waiting for the server's preview of this unit.

migration.materializeIrreversible_one: Creates {n} object in the world at the placed position. All or nothing: if one fails, everything this unit created is removed again.
migration.materializeIrreversible_other: Creates {n} objects in the world at the placed position. All or nothing: if one fails, everything this unit created is removed again.
migration.materializeUnconfirmed: Materialize was not confirmed. It may have created objects; the list was read again.
migration.maxUnits: A migration holds at most {max} units.
migration.moreUnlisted_one: and {n} more object the server did not list: its console has them all
migration.moreUnlisted_other: and {n} more objects the server did not list: its console has them all

migration.noSourceGroups: The server lists no groups for the source version {version}: it holds none, or it can no longer be read.
migration.noUnitsBody: A unit is one group of the source version. Add one, place it in the world, then materialize it.
migration.offMap: This migration targets {target}, and the server is running {map}. Only deleting it works from here.
migration.offMapNote: You are on {map}. This migration can only be worked on from {target}; only deleting it works here.
migration.placeIntroAim: The server previews {name} at where you aim, and its members are drawn there as ghosts. Placing creates nothing: it records where Materialize will create the objects.

restore.moreBlockers_one: {count} more blocker. The blocked operations are in the list.

restore.excludedNote: Left exactly as they are now. Excluded objects are never counted as verified, so verifying this restore reports each one the version holds as unverified.
restore.leftAloneNote: These domains are not part of this version, so nothing in them is touched: {domains}.
restore.onRestoreNote: A recovery version is captured first, so the restore can be rolled back. The server then re-plans from a fresh capture and refuses, changing nothing, if this fingerprint no longer matches.
restore.applyRecovery: A recovery version is captured first, so this restore can be rolled back. The server then re-plans from a fresh capture and refuses, changing nothing, if the world moved since this plan.
restore.applyExcluded_one: {count} object is excluded and stays exactly as it is now.
restore.applyExcluded_other: {count} objects are excluded and stay exactly as they are now.
restore.applyChurn: The session change is acknowledged: session-scoped objects are removed and rebuilt with new identities.
restore.applyOneTick: It runs in one server tick with no progress to report: the server answers once, when it is done.

restore.historyNoMatch_one: None of the {count} operations matches the search or the map filter.

restore.interruptedElsewhere: This restore did not finish on {map}. It blocks restores on that map only, and the server resolves it only while it runs that map.
restore.isRollbackOf: A rollback: it restored the recovery version captured before {link} ran.
restore.abandonedAt: Abandoned {when}. Abandoning changed nothing in the world.

restore.rolledBackBy: Rolled back by {link}. A rollback is a new restore, so this one keeps its own status; verifying it now compares the world with a target it was rolled back from.
restore.remaining_one: {count} inconsistency remain from this operation. Manual intervention is required.
restore.remaining_other: {count} inconsistencies remain from this operation. Manual intervention is required.
restore.actionsNote: Roll back runs at once, with no plan to review. Review a rollback first plans a restore to the recovery version instead, with its counts, blockers and fingerprint.

restore.rollbackIrreversible: Returns the world to {recovery}, the recovery version captured before {id} ran, with no new review: anything changed since then is overwritten.

restore.rollbackRecorded: A new recovery version is captured before anything changes, and the rollback is recorded as a new restore, so it can be rolled back in turn.
restore.resolveRollbackIrreversible: Returns the world to {recovery}, the recovery version captured before {id} started, with no new review: what it changed before it stopped is undone, and anything changed since is overwritten.
restore.resolveRollbackReport: Report what is inconsistent shows what this would change, and writes nothing.

restore.abandonNote: Do this only once you have checked the world. Report what is inconsistent shows how far it is from the recovery version.

deploy.forgetBody: '{target}' is recorded as owned by this deployment and is not on this server. Forgetting clears the ownership record only. Nothing in the world is touched. The server checks the object is really gone before it writes anything.

deploy.recoverBody: Only the objects THIS run touched are returned. It is not a whole-world restore, and it is never itself recovered.
deploy.claimBody: This run created objects and never recorded that it owns them. Claiming adopts them from the run's own journal. Nothing is guessed, matched or scored. Without it the next deployment creates a second copy of everything.

deploy.abandonBody: Anything it created stays, unowned, and no future deployment will modify or remove it. Anything it removed stays removed.

deployRun.headRecoverRefused: The recovery was refused. Nothing was changed.
deployRun.headClaimed_one: Claimed {count} object. This deployment now owns them.
deployRun.headClaimed_other: Claimed {count} objects. This deployment now owns them.
deployRun.headClaimPartialOne_one: Claimed {claimed} object; {count} object could not be claimed.
deployRun.headClaimPartialOne_other: Claimed {claimed} object; {count} objects could not be claimed.
deployRun.headClaimPartial_one: Claimed {claimed} objects; {count} object could not be claimed.

deployRun.headClaimRefused: The claim was refused. Nothing was changed.
deployRun.headAbandonRefused: The run could not be abandoned.
deployRun.listLoading: Reading the deployments on this map
deployRun.listEmptyBody: A deployment applies a Version captured on another server to this one, and remembers what it created so the next deployment can tell its own objects from everything else here.
deployRun.lastAnswerShown: {error} What is shown is the last answer.
deployRun.listCapped: The server lists at most {n} deployments and says nothing about the rest. Search covers the listed ones only.
deployRun.deleteBlockedLoading: Its run history is loading; an unresolved run would block the delete.
deployRun.bandUncommitted: Needs a person. Run {run} changed the world and never recorded what it owns. Resolve it before deploying again.
deployRun.bandInterrupted: Needs a person. Run {run} did not finish. Resolve it before deploying again.
deployRun.targetMismatchNote: This deployment's target ids belong to another installation, so it cannot prove what it owns here. Adopt it only if this server IS that server.
deployRun.archivedNote: Archived. It accepts no new runs, and the version it last deployed stays pinned. Restore it from the archive to deploy again.
deployRun.heldNote: A held object is in scope, has no target, and this deployment claims nothing for it. A deployment carrying a hold never reports a clean verification.
deployRun.scopeFrozenNote: Frozen when it was created. Nothing outside it is ever matched, modified or removed.
deployRun.deleteNote: Deleting a deployment never removes live objects, and the server refuses it while the deployment owns any.
deployRun.planLoading: Planning on the server: it captures the whole world and probes every adapter. Nothing is changed
deployRun.planFailedTitle: The server did not plan this
deployRun.planErrorBandStale: {heading}. {body} The plan below is no longer what the server would run. Deploy stays shut until a plan arrives.
deployRun.staleBand: This plan is out of date: the server answered that it changed since it was reviewed. Nothing was changed. Re-plan it.
deployRun.refusedBand: The server refused the deployment. Nothing was changed. {reasons}
deployRun.blockedBand_one: This plan is blocked: {count} blocker, listed in the inspector. Nothing can be deployed until every one is resolved.
deployRun.blockedBand_other: This plan is blocked: {count} blockers, listed in the inspector. Nothing can be deployed until every one is resolved.
deployRun.blockedBandMore_one: This plan is blocked: {count} blocker or more, listed in the inspector. Nothing can be deployed until every one is resolved.
deployRun.blockedBandMore_other: This plan is blocked: {count} blockers or more, listed in the inspector. Nothing can be deployed until every one is resolved.
deployRun.noopBand: Nothing to change. This server already matches version {version} inside this deployment's scope, so there is nothing to deploy.
deployRun.sourceChangesCap: between the deployed Version and this one
deployRun.driftCap: changed here, inside what this deployment owns
deployRun.actionsCap: recreate is part of create, not extra
deployRun.ackDropped: The numbers changed when the plan was made again, so the earlier tick no longer applies. Read it again.
deployRun.replanHint: The plan on screen was made with different acknowledgements. Re-plan so the server plans with the ones ticked here; they are part of what Deploy sends.
deployRun.opsErrorTitle: The operation list could not be read
deployRun.opsErrorBody: {error} The plan above is unchanged, and it is what Deploy sends: the server checks its fingerprint again before it changes anything. Re-plan to read the operations again.
deployRun.nothingToChangeBody: This server already matches the source version inside this deployment's scope. There is nothing to deploy.
deployRun.groupOpNote: A Group operation names the source Group; the Group it writes here gets its own id.
deployRun.blockersCap: The server sends at most {n} blockers.
deployRun.dryRunNote: A plan is a dry run: nothing has been changed. Deploy sends this plan's fingerprint, and the server plans again from its own capture and refuses if anything it covers moved.
deployRun.historyEmptyBody: This deployment has not been applied. Plan it against a Version captured on the source server to see what it would do here.
deployRun.scopeEmptyBody: This deployment names no Groups and no objects, so there is nothing for it to deploy.
deployRun.ownedEmptyBody: Ownership is recorded when a run commits. Nothing has been deployed from this stream yet, or the last run did not commit its mapping.
deployRun.openOneUncommitted: Run {run} needs a person: it changed the world and never recorded what it owns. Every plan and apply on this map is blocked until it is resolved.
deployRun.openOneInterrupted: Run {run} needs a person: it did not finish. Every plan and apply on this map is blocked until it is resolved.
deployRun.openManyUncommitted_one: {count} run need a person: it changed the world and never recorded what it owns. Every plan and apply on this map is blocked until it is resolved.
deployRun.openManyUncommitted_other: {count} runs need a person: it changed the world and never recorded what it owns. Every plan and apply on this map is blocked until it is resolved.
deployRun.openManyInterrupted_one: {count} run need a person: it did not finish. Every plan and apply on this map is blocked until it is resolved.
deployRun.openManyInterrupted_other: {count} runs need a person: it did not finish. Every plan and apply on this map is blocked until it is resolved.
deployRun.incompleteBand: Run {run} could not return every object it touched. It does not block this map, but a person has to finish its recovery.
deployRun.runsCapped: Up to {n} runs shown, newest first: the server lists no more.
deployRun.scopeCut: Showing {groups} of {groupsTotal} Groups and {objects} of {objectsTotal} standalone objects: the server cuts this list to fit one reply.
deployRun.holdsCut: The server lists {n} of {total} holds, so an object marked "hold not listed" may still be held.
deployRun.runUncommittedBand: Not committed. This run changed the world and never recorded what it owns.
deployRun.runInterruptedBand: Interrupted. This run did not finish. Resolve it before deploying again.
deployRun.resolveNote: Report writes nothing. Each of the others is confirmed first and changes what the server records about this run.
deployRun.remainingNote_one: {count} inconsistency remain from this run. Recovery is incomplete and a person has to finish it.
deployRun.remainingNote_other: {count} inconsistencies remain from this run. Recovery is incomplete and a person has to finish it.
deployRun.earlierVersionNote: Deploying an earlier version is an ordinary run: it is planned, reviewed and confirmed like any other.
deployRun.groupWholeNote: A Group is deployed whole, as the unit the engine deploys. Its members cannot be held one by one from here.
deployRun.heldObjectNote: A held object is in scope, has no target here, and this deployment claims nothing for it. It is the only way past an object its adapter cannot create, and it never counts towards a clean verification. An object this deployment already owns cannot be held.
deployRun.holdButton: Hold: do not deploy this object
deployRun.scopeFrozenLongNote: Scope is frozen when a deployment is created. It cannot be widened later, because widening it would either lose the ownership record or claim objects this deployment never made.
deployRun.forgetLostSession: Its identity only lasted one server session; the next deployment creates it again and records the new id. There is nothing to forget.
deployRun.forgetPresent: It is on this server. Forget only drops the record of an object that is genuinely gone.
deployRun.mappingIntro: One row per object this deployment owns. This is a support view: a source id and a target id are two different things in two different identity namespaces, and this is where you can see the pairing.
deployRun.missingNote: This object should have survived a restart and is not here. Something removed it. Nothing is planned for its source object until a person forgets the record.
deployRun.lostSessionNote: Its identity only lasts for one server session, so the id it was created with is gone. The next deployment creates it again and records the new id.

remote.proseQueued: Vetra is holding this for the target server. It will start as soon as that server next checks in.
remote.proseClaimed: The target server has taken this on and is about to fetch the package.
remote.proseDownloading: The target server is fetching the package from Vetra and checking it against its digest.
remote.prosePlanning: The target server is working out what would change. Nothing on it has been modified.
remote.proseAwaitingApproval: The target server has worked out exactly what would change. Read it below and approve if it is what you want. Nothing has been modified yet.
remote.proseApproved: You approved this plan. The target server will apply it the next time it checks in.
remote.proseApplying: The target server is changing its world now. It took a recovery snapshot first, and this cannot be cancelled.
remote.prosePlanStale: The target server's world changed after you approved, so nothing was applied. A new plan is being prepared and will need your approval again.
remote.proseSucceeded: The target server applied this and verified the result against the Version.
remote.proseFailed: This did not complete. Nothing on the target is half-finished. See the reason below.
remote.proseCancelled: You cancelled this before anything was applied.
remote.proseRecoveryRequired: The target server was interrupted while applying. Its own recovery has to be run there by an administrator before it will deploy again. Nothing will be re-applied automatically.
remote.proseExpired: Nobody acted on this before its window closed. Nothing was applied. Prepare it again if you still want it.
remote.failTransportFailed: The package could not be moved to the target server. This is a network or storage problem and says nothing about your licence. Try again.
remote.failPackageInvalid: The package arrived on the target server and was not readable as a Vetra package. Export the Version again.
remote.failPlanBlocked: The target server could not produce a plan it was willing to run. Open Deploy on that server to see what is blocking it.
remote.failMapMismatch: The target server is running a different map from the one this Version was captured on. Remote deployment is same-map.
remote.failApplyFailed: The target server could not finish applying. It ran its own recovery; check Deploy on that server.
remote.failVerificationFailed: The target server applied the changes and could not verify the result matched the Version. Check Deploy on that server.
remote.failAttemptSuperseded: The target server restarted while working on this. Nothing was applied. Prepare it again.
remote.failExpired: This was not started before its window closed.
remote.failNothingToDeploy: The target server already matches this Version, so there was nothing to deploy. This is not a problem.
remote.failTargetUnavailable: The target server cannot run Blueprints right now.
remote.failAuthorizationLost: Vetra will not authorize this at the moment. Check that both servers are enabled and licensed for Blueprints.
remote.failProtocolError: The target server and Vetra disagreed about this deployment. Nothing was applied.
remote.failFallback: This stopped for a reason this build does not have wording for. Contact Vetra with the deployment reference above.
remote.promptList: Select a deployment to see what it is doing, or start a new one.
remote.promptPick: Choose the version to send. Nothing leaves this server until you confirm.
remote.promptTarget: Choose the server to send it to. Nothing there changes until you approve its plan here.
remote.platformUnreadableBody: Something replied at Vetra's address, but the reply was not Vetra's, so this is the address this server is pointed at rather than your connection or your licence. Your Versions and the local Deploy screen are unaffected. ({error})
remote.platformRefusedBody: The connection worked, so this is not an outage. Your Versions and the local Deploy screen are unaffected. This is remote deployment only. ({error})
remote.platformOfflineBody: Your Versions and the local Deploy screen are unaffected. This is remote deployment only, and it is a connectivity problem rather than anything about your licence. ({error})
remote.platformLineOffline: Vetra could not be reached ({error}). Your local Versions and Deploy are unaffected.
remote.platformLineUnreadable: Something that is not Vetra answered at its address ({error}). Your local Versions and Deploy are unaffected.
remote.platformLineRefused: Vetra declined this request ({error}). Your local Versions and Deploy are unaffected.
remote.emptyBody: A remote deployment puts a Version from this server onto another of your servers: Vetra carries the package, that server works out exactly what would change, and nothing is applied until you approve it here.
remote.eolHeading: Remote Deploy is not part of this build
remote.eolBody: This build of Blueprints runs without Vetra licensing, so this server holds no credential Vetra accepts and every remote request is refused before it is sent. Remote Deploy is carried by Vetra and cannot work without it. Your Versions and the local Deploy screen are unaffected; to move a Version to another server, export it as a package file and import it there.
remote.credentialHeading: Vetra does not accept this server's credential
remote.credentialBody: This server holds no machine credential Vetra accepts, so Remote Deploy is unavailable until the server is activated or recovered from the server console. The licence state says which. This is not an outage, and your Versions and the local Deploy screen are unaffected.
remote.refusalNoVersions: This server has no Versions of its own to deploy. Capture one first.
remote.refusalNoTargets: Vetra lists no other server on your licence that can receive a deployment. Activate the target server first.
remote.refusalChooseBoth: Choose a Version and a target server.
remote.refusalNoPlan: There is no plan to review yet.
remote.holdCooldown: The server takes one remote request every 4 s, and this page waits 4.35 s to be sure. Wait a moment.
remote.holdUnknown: The server has not answered the last remote request. Wait a moment before sending another.
remote.ackDriftTitle_one: Overwrite {count} change(s) made on the target server
remote.ackDriftTitle_other: Overwrite {count} change(s) made on the target server
remote.ackDriftBody_one: {count} object(s) this deployment manages were changed ON THE TARGET SERVER since it last deployed. Approving replaces those changes with this Version's values.
remote.ackDriftBody_other: {count} object(s) this deployment manages were changed ON THE TARGET SERVER since it last deployed. Approving replaces those changes with this Version's values.
remote.ackDriftMissing_one: {count} more are missing from the target entirely.
remote.ackDriftMissing_other: {count} more are missing from the target entirely.
remote.ackChurnTitle: Remove and rebuild objects with new identities
remote.ackChurnBody: This server restarted between the Version the target last deployed and this one, so objects it manages are not in this Version under any identity it recognises. Approving REMOVES them from the target and creates whatever this Version contains. Nothing is matched by position, model or name.
remote.ackScopeTitle: Deploy without Group(s) the target is scoped to
remote.ackScopeBody: The target server's deployment is scoped to Group(s) this Version does not contain. Nothing is deployed for them. Read the Remove count before approving.
remote.ackBaselineBody: The target server could not read the Version it last deployed, so it cannot tell a source change from a change made on the target. Every operation is reported as target drift, which is the most alarming reading, and none is suppressed.
remote.blockedEol: Remote Deploy is not part of this build.
remote.blockedCredential: Vetra does not accept this server's credential.
remote.blockedFirstAnswer: Waiting for the server's first answer.
remote.blockedPlatform: Vetra did not answer the last read, so a deployment cannot start. Refresh once it does.
remote.blockedPreparing: A remote deployment is already being prepared on this server. Wait for it to finish.
remote.blockedNotSelectable: That server's reference is not one this server can send to.
remote.blockedNotAwaiting: This deployment is not waiting for approval.
remote.blockedNoFingerprint: This plan carries no fingerprint, so the server would refuse the approval. Refresh and review it again.
remote.blockedPlanBlockers: This plan has blockers that must be resolved on the target server before it can be approved.
remote.blockedTicks_one: Tick every required acknowledgement first: {count} of {total} ticked.
remote.blockedTicks_other: Tick every required acknowledgement first: {count} of {total} ticked.
remote.approveIrreversible: This permanently removes {removed} object(s) from {target}, and it cannot be cancelled once it starts.
remote.approveIrreversibleDrift: This permanently removes {removed} object(s) from {target} and overwrites {drift} change(s) made there, and it cannot be cancelled once it starts.
remote.approveIrreversibleUnnamed: This permanently removes {removed} object(s) from the target server, and it cannot be cancelled once it starts.
remote.approveIrreversibleDriftUnnamed: This permanently removes {removed} object(s) from the target server and overwrites {drift} change(s) made there, and it cannot be cancelled once it starts.
remote.noticeUnconfirmedPrepare: The server did not confirm the prepare.
remote.noticeUnconfirmedApproval: The server did not confirm the approval of {reference}.
remote.noticeUnconfirmedCancel: The server did not confirm the cancellation of {reference}.
remote.noticeUnreadablePrepare: The answer to the prepare could not be read.
remote.noticeUnreadableApproval: The answer to the approval of {reference} could not be read.
remote.noticeUnreadableCancel: The answer to the cancellation of {reference} could not be read.
remote.noticeMayHaveRun: It may have gone through, and nothing was sent again. The list has been read again: check what it says before deciding.
remote.noticeFailedPrepare: The prepare did not go through. {heading}. {body}
remote.noticeFailedApproval: The approval of {reference} did not go through. {heading}. {body}
remote.noticeFailedCancel: The cancellation of {reference} did not go through. {heading}. {body}
remote.noticeAcksCleared: The target server published a new plan for {reference}, so every acknowledgement was cleared. Read the new plan before approving.
remote.noticeDialogStale: {reference} changed while the confirmation was open (it now reads {status}). Nothing was sent. Review it again.
remote.readFailedLast: {heading}. {body} What is shown arrived at the last read.
remote.pickTitle: New remote deployment: choose the Version
remote.pickNote: Only Versions this server captured are listed: a Version from another installation is deployed from the server that captured it.
remote.pickCapped: Up to {count} are shown, newest first.
remote.targetTitle: New remote deployment: choose the target server
remote.planGoneHeading: This plan is no longer listed
remote.planGoneBody: Vetra lists up to {count} of the most recent deployments this server started, and this one is not among them now, or it no longer carries a plan.
remote.listCapped: Up to {count} deployments are shown: Vetra lists the most recent ones this server started.
remote.sameMapNote: Remote deployment is same-map: the target server refuses a Version captured on another map.
remote.preparedNotice: {reference} is prepared. {target} works out the plan when it next checks in, and the plan then waits here for your approval.
remote.preparedUnreadNotice: The server prepared it, though its answer could not be read. {target} works out the plan when it next checks in, and the plan then waits here for your approval.
remote.prepareBody: Vetra will package {version} and send it to {target}. That server will work out what would change and show you the plan. Nothing on {target} changes until you approve that plan.
remote.prepareProgress: This server exports the Version and uploads it, which can take a few minutes. Its progress is read from the server every 5 s.
remote.approvedNotice: Approved {reference}. {target} applies it the next time it checks in.
remote.approvedNoticeUnnamed: Approved {reference}. The target server applies it the next time it checks in.
remote.approveBody: The target server will take a recovery snapshot, apply this plan and verify the result. Once it starts, it cannot be cancelled.
remote.cancelBody: The target server will stop working on this. Nothing it has already done is undone, because nothing has been applied.
remote.preparingNote: Any administrator's prepare shows here: this server prepares one remote deployment at a time.
remote.targetRunNote: The target run is the id of this deployment in Deploy on {target}.
remote.diagNotPollingNote: This server is not asking Vetra for deployments sent to it. It polls only while Blueprints is allowed here and the server holds a machine credential.
remote.planNotAwaiting: This deployment reads “{state}”, so there is nothing to approve here.
remote.planNotAwaitingUnknown: This deployment reads a state this build has no word for, so there is nothing to approve here.
remote.planBlockedBand: This plan has blockers that must be resolved on the target server before it can be approved. The target plans again by itself once they are.
remote.blockOnTargetCaption: changed there since it last deployed
remote.blockEffectCaption: on the target server, once you approve
remote.firstDeployment: This is the first deployment to that server: it has no deployed baseline yet.
remote.acksNote: Each one is a decision about that server. A new plan from the target clears every tick.
remote.notesNone: The target server reported no blockers and no warnings.
remote.unreadableList: the server sent a Remote Deploy list this page cannot read
remote.unreadableAnswer: the server sent an answer this page cannot read

adapters.capSnapshot: Can be captured into a version
adapters.capMaterialize: Can be recreated from a version
adapters.capProperties: Captured settings can be written back
adapters.capRemove: Can be deleted during a restore
adapters.capUnknown: Declared by the adapter; this version of Blueprints does not name it.
adapters.identityPersistent: Its objects keep the same identity across a server restart.
adapters.identitySession: Its objects keep their identity only until the server restarts.
adapters.identityWeak: Its objects may change identity at any time.
adapters.unavailableCost: Objects in this domain cannot be captured, and any version that recorded them cannot be restored until this is fixed.
adapters.presenceUnknown: This server's Blueprints does not say whether an addon is simply not installed, so every unavailable adapter below is listed as needing attention, including those whose addon you do not run. Update Blueprints on the server to tell them apart.
adapters.disabledMeaning: Captures leave this adapter out, and a restore or deployment that would change its objects refuses those objects, until it is enabled again. Nothing already captured is changed.
adapters.absentMeaning: The addon this adapter integrates with is not installed on this server. Nothing needs doing: the adapter starts working when the addon is installed.
adapters.intentMissing: No adapter {id} is registered on this server now.
adapters.title: Adapters
adapters.emptyBody: The overview that carries the registry has not arrived. Ask again if it does not appear.
adapters.noneBody: Blueprints has nothing to capture. Install an adapter, or check the server console for a registration error.
adapters.noneInstalledTitle: None of these addons is installed
adapters.noneInstalledBody_one: Blueprints ships {n} adapters, and the addons they integrate with are not on this server. Nothing needs doing.
adapters.noneInstalledBody_other: Blueprints ships {n} adapters, and the addons they integrate with are not on this server. Nothing needs doing.
adapters.staleAt: {heading}. The registry below was read at {time}.
adapters.staleEarlier: {heading}. The registry below was read at an earlier moment.
adapters.enableAnyTime: You can enable it again here at any time.
adapters.enableConfirmBody: Captures include this adapter again from now on, when its addon is available. Versions captured while it was disabled still know nothing about its objects.

host.failUpdateGame: Blueprints needs the Chromium browser Garry's Mod embeds: update the game.
host.failNotAffected: The server and its players are not affected.
host.failFiles: Vetra Blueprints cannot open: {reason}. Reconnect to the server. If this happens again, the server's vetra-blueprints folder is incomplete or mixes two versions: reinstall it.
host.failStart: Vetra Blueprints could not start its interface: {reason}. Nothing on the server was changed.
